teachingReview.heading: Coordinate voriconazole with meals and tube feeds
teachingReview.body: Give oral voriconazole on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or one hour after a meal. With tube feeding, hold the feed for one hour before and one hour after each dose. Write the dose and feeding times together so the interruption is visible to everyone administering them. This schedule is specific to voriconazole; do not copy it to itraconazole or posaconazole products.

teachingReview.heading: Build the food and pH plan around the formulation
teachingReview.body: Itraconazole capsules are taken with food, while the oral solution is taken on an empty stomach. Conventional Sporanox capsules require an acidic environment, so antacids and acid-suppressing medicines can reduce absorption. Posaconazole oral suspension is taken with a full meal or an oral liquid nutritional supplement; PPIs and cimetidine can decrease its absorption. Confirm the exact product and review these medicines when building the administration plan. Suspension and delayed-release tablets are not interchangeable, so changing formulation requires a new dosing review.

teachingReview.heading: Reject dose-for-dose substitution
teachingReview.body: Posaconazole suspension and delayed-release tablets differ in bioavailability, food effects, and dosing. Itraconazole solution and capsules also have different absorption requirements.

retainedBodies.heading: Coordinate voriconazole with meals and tube feeds
retainedBodies.body: Give oral voriconazole on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or one hour after a meal. With tube feeding, hold the feed for one hour before and one hour after each dose. Write the dose and feeding times together so the interruption is visible to everyone administering them. This schedule is specific to voriconazole; do not copy it to itraconazole or posaconazole products.

retainedBodies.heading: Build the food and pH plan around the formulation
retainedBodies.body: Itraconazole capsules are taken with food, while the oral solution is taken on an empty stomach. Conventional Sporanox capsules require an acidic environment, so antacids and acid-suppressing medicines can reduce absorption. Posaconazole oral suspension is taken with a full meal or an oral liquid nutritional supplement; PPIs and cimetidine can decrease its absorption. Confirm the exact product and review these medicines when building the administration plan. Suspension and delayed-release tablets are not interchangeable, so changing formulation requires a new dosing review.

retainedBodies.heading: Reject dose-for-dose substitution
retainedBodies.body: Posaconazole suspension and delayed-release tablets differ in bioavailability, food effects, and dosing. Itraconazole solution and capsules also have different absorption requirements.
